short: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow

title.title: Calabi flow can blow up in finite time
title.subtitle: Claim: a $U(10)$-invariant metric on $\mathbb{CP}^{10}$ whose Calabi flow develops a point singularity

plain: A flow meant to smooth a shape toward its ideal form can tear in finite time, even when a perfect form exists

beats.text: Calabi flow, fourth order, should carry any Kähler metric toward a canonical one
Chen conjectured it exists for all time. Here it stops at a finite time $T_*$
Scalar curvature grows like $(T_*-t)^{-1/2}$, though the class holds Fubini–Study

steps: Start from a very symmetric metric on complex projective space
Symmetry turns the flow into an equation in one variable
Its solution pinches to a point in finite time

achievement.label: Chen's long-time existence conjecture for Calabi flow
statement: \exists\, g_0 \text{ on } \mathbb{CP}^{10}:\ T_* < \infty,\ R \sim a\,(T_* - t)^{-1/2}
achievement.context: Products give examples in every complex dimension from 10 up, in classes with Kähler–Einstein metrics
achievement.note: Only in complex dimension 10 and up; 54 pages, no Lean

verify.detail: No Lean: a 54-page manuscript, reduced by symmetry to one radial variable
verify.ourCheck: We read the paper's strategy; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Calabi flow should carry any metric toward a canonical one. Chen said forever.
Symmetry reduces it to one variable, which pinches to a point.
Claimed: a finite time singularity, in ten dimensions.

sources.quote: There is a smooth U(10)-invariant Kaehler metric on CP^10 in the Fubini-Study class whose Calabi flow has a finite maximal existence time T* with scalar curvature at a point ~ a (T* - t)^{-1/2}; products give examples in every complex dimension >= 10 in classes with Kaehler-Einstein metrics.

sources.quote: Chen conjectured that the Calabi flow, a fourth-order flow toward constant scalar curvature, exists for all time from any smooth Kähler metric
